diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore, $D\cR (u)$ is invertible with $\| (D\cR (u))^{-1}\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.
Therefore any $A\in D\cR (u)$ satisfies $\|A^{-1}\|_\infty \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.

issues.failure_explanation: An eigenvalue-modulus bound only gives a bound on the spectral radius of $A^{-1}$, not on any operator norm; the inference 'eigenvalues have modulus $\ge\mu$, therefore $\|A^{-1}\|\le1/\mu$' is invalid, and the norm is unspecified. It is false in the spectral norm even with the paper's sign structure: $A=[[11,-10],[0,1]]$ is $1$-diagonally dominant with non-positive off-diagonals yet $\|A^{-1}\|_2\approx1.35>1$. The $\ell^\infty$ version used later in Theorem thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen is true, but requires a different standard argument (Varah-type bound) that the source never gives.

failure_location.quote: By Gershgorin theorem, if $A$ is $\mu$-diagonally dominant, all the eigenvalues of $A$ have complex modulus bigger or equal than $\mu$, and therefore, $A$ is invertible with $\| A^{-1}\| \leq \frac{1}{\mu}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Gershgorin-to-norm step by the standard direct argument (or Varah's bound) proving $\|(D\cR(u))^{-1}\|_\infty\le1/\mu$, and state the norm explicitly in the lemma.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's invertibility and eigenvalue conclusions stand, and the downstream Hadamard/Pourciau arguments in thm:exist-uniqueness-scheme-gen survive once the $\ell^\infty$ bound is correctly established; but as written the stated norm bound is unproven and false under the natural spectral-norm reading, leaving the uniform inverse bound used throughout Section 2 unestablished in the source.
issues.title: Invalid Gershgorin-to-norm inference in the Jacobian invertibility lemma
issues.why_classification: Routine local repair: the conclusion is true in the $\ell^\infty$ norm via a standard three-line argument, and every downstream use (Hadamard, Pourciau, eigenvalue discussion in Section 5.1) survives with it.

issues.failure_explanation: The Proposition hypothesizes a function $u$ satisfying $\cH(x,u(x),\hD u(x))=\cR(u)(x)$ for $x\in\mO$, but $\hD u(x)$ and $\cR(u)(x)$ are defined in the source only at graph nodes (via the neighbor sets $\cV_j$); for $x\in\mO$ off the nodes, and hence for the right-hand side $\|R(u)\|_{L^\infty(\mO)}$, these objects are undefined. In the general geometrical-graph setting of Section 2 the stated objects cannot even be constructed; they are well defined only under extra structure (e.g. uniform Cartesian grids with a shifted-grid residual), which the source does not provide.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict to uniform Cartesian grids and define $\cR(u)(x)$ for all $x$ via the shifted-grid construction so that nodal residuals coincide with the scheme's, or weaken the right-hand side to the nodal residual $\max_{j\in\cJ}|\cH(x_j,u(x_j),\hD_G u(x_j))|$, and complete the comparison-principle proof.

issues.why_classification: Repairing requires a nontrivial definitional construction plus a setting restriction, or a limited weakening of the stated estimate; both are contained and leave a comparable a posteriori bound, so neither minor (advertised scope does not survive a purely local edit) nor serious.

\|u^{n}-v^{n}\|_\infty \leq \|u^0 - v^0\|_\infty + \sum_{1\leq m\leq n} \max\big(\dt \|\cR(u)^{m}\|_\infty, \|\bar b^{m}-\bar c^{m}\|_{\ell^\infty(\cB)} \big)

issues.failure_explanation: Under the defined hypotheses (F1)-(F3), which allow $\partial_u\cF\ge-\lambda/\dt<0$, the claimed one-step estimate is false. Counterexample: one interior node, $\cF(x,u,p)=-u$, $\dt=1/2$ (so (F3) holds with $\lambda=1/2$), $u^0=v^0=0$, equal boundary data, residual $\cR(u)^1=r>0$; the schemes give $u^1=r$, $v^1=0$, so the left side is $r$ while the claimed right side is $0+\max(r/2,0)=r/2$. The proof is a single sentence deferring to 'similar arguments'; the stationary comparison argument applied here yields only the weaker bound with factor $1/(1-\lambda)$, i.e. $\max_j(u^{n+1}_j-v^{n+1}_j)_+\le(\|u^n-v^n\|_\infty+\dt\|\cR(u)^{n+1}\|_\infty)/(1-\lambda)$, reflecting genuine amplification for anti-monotone $\cF$ (as for $u_t=u$). issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the hypothesis $\partial_u\cF\ge0$ (which makes (F3) vacuous) or restate the estimate with the factor $1/(1-\lambda)$ (with $\lambda=\dt\,c$ giving $e^{cT}$-type accumulated constants), and supply the omitted comparison-principle proof; adjust the recursion accordingly.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In Lemma~\ref{lem:DR-invertible}, we derived a lower bound for $\mu_h$ to be $O(h)$ so the condition number $$\kappa_h := \frac{C_h}{\mu_h} = O(h^{-1}).$$
where we used \(\log(1/q_h^2)\sim 2/\kappa_h\) for large \(\kappa_h\)
This shows that ``warm starting'' does reduce the total number of needed iterations.

issues.failure_explanation: Three defects in this analysis: (i) $\kappa_h:=C_h/\mu_h$ is declared $O(h^{-1})$ together with $\mu_h=O(h)$, but $C_h$ is the smoothness constant of the squared-residual loss, $C_h\approx\sigma_{\max}(D\cR)^2$, which scales like $1/h$ (the Jacobian entries are $\sim(1/\sqrt M)(1/h)$), so $C_h/\mu_h=(\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min})^2=O(h^{-2})$; $O(h^{-1})$ is the condition number of $D\cR$, a different object. (ii) The rate $E_k\le(1-\kappa_h^{-1})^{2k}E_0$ is not implied by the stated assumptions (smoothness plus quadratic growth, with no convexity); the guaranteed rate under strong convexity is $(1-\kappa^{-1})^k$, the exponent $2k$ being specific to quadratics. (iii) The symbol $q_h$ in the iteration-count formula is never defined. Consequently the predicted iteration counts ($\approx(\kappa_h/2)\log(E_0/\texttt{tol})$), the net-gain magnitudes, and the concluding claim that warm starting 'does reduce the total number of needed iterations' are not established by the displayed formulas.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the derivation consistently: fix the $\kappa_h$ scaling to $O(h^{-2})$ as defined (or redefine $\kappa_h$ as cond($D\cR$) and adjust), use the provable $(1-\kappa^{-1})^k$ rate or assume quadratic structure, define $q_h$, and derive positivity of the net gain under explicit assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative iteration-complexity predictions of the warm-start subsection are unreliable; the qualitative conclusions (conditioning worsens under grid refinement, warm starting helps) survive.
issues.title: Warm-start convergence-rate analysis is internally inconsistent and unsupported
issues.why_classification: Heuristic subsection with a local re-derivation; the qualitative claims and the multilevel strategy survive, and no formal result depends on the constants.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the monotonicity conditions (H1)-(H3) ensure convergence of the residual minimization for the HJBI example. But the example's equation (eq:HJBI) and its listed discretizations contain no zeroth-order term in $u$, so the scheme's Hamiltonian has $\partial\cH/\partial u=0$ and violates (H3), which requires $\partial\cH/\partial u\ge\lambda>0$ (the paper itself adds a $\lambda u_j$ damping term precisely for this purpose in Section 5.1); the drift term $-v_cu_x$ is not discretized in the source at all, so even (H2) is unverifiable. The paper's well-posedness and critical-point-uniqueness theory therefore does not apply to this example, and no guarantee of convergence to the physically relevant weak solution is established for it.
